title: Population of the Californias
subtitle: Padrones, censos and mission registros, 1777–1847 — every count so far transcribed from the Archives of California, each linked to its record
abstract: The population counts of Spanish and Mexican California, settlement by settlement, as the archive recorded them. A note on what these numbers are: they are the counts of a colonial bureaucracy. Padrones undercount, categories like gente de razon and neofito are the empire's constructs, and Native people appear only when and how the state counted them — inside missions, pueblos, and jurisdictions. The map shows what the documents say, in their own units, not how many people lived in California; the nations of the Native California map were mostly never counted at all. Every row cites its document. The headline: in 1790 the entire Spanish population of Alta California was 910 people.
legend_note: Figures are the documents' own; categories are the colonial state's. Click any citation to open the catalog record for that document. This is a growing selection of the archive's counts, not a complete census of them.

features.name: Alta California (province-wide counts)
features.summary: The whole colony, counted. In 1790 the entire Spanish population of Alta California was 910 people, inside a mission population of 7,353. The cumulative mission ledgers then state the system's demographic arithmetic: by 1817, 64,675 baptized against 41,757 dead; by Durán's 1833 cuadro — covering the 13 southern (Fernandino) missions only, after the Zacatecan split — 52,882 baptized, 38,417 dead, 10,482 living.
series: 8,323 souls total: 910 gente de razon + 7,353 Indios (per-establishment table)
10,638 souls in Alta California, per-settlement (up from 8,323 in 1790)

1,275 gente de razón in the whole of Alta California — 4 presidios + 2 pueblos; of these only 368 were vecinos, the rest military families
St. Pap., Sacramento (C-A 56) Doc 378 — province-wide census of both Californias
mission almas: 3,465 (1795) and 5,322[?] (1796) for Alta California, queried against the Baja returns

features.name: Mission San Fernando Rey
features.summary: Founded 1797 in the valley north of Los Ángeles, and the northern anchor of the Santa Bárbara district's returns.
series: counted in the 1814 friar roster; ministers Muñoz & Oliva
named in the Santa Bárbara jurisdiction *estado*: the district held 2,854 souls, of whom ~2,348 Indians
surveyed in the 1834 statistical questionnaire for the Mexican national statistics — terrain, routes, buildings, orchards, and 60 barrels of aguardiente with the Tujunga acequia
Dep. St. Pap., Benicia (C-A 20) Doc 223 — 'Nota analítica sobre la formación de la estadística'
sold outright to Eulogio Célis for $14,000
St. Pap., Missions (C-A 51) Doc 161 — the consolidated record of Pico's mission alienations

sources.citation: Every row cites its own document in the Archives of California; follow the link to the catalog record.

features.name: Mission Santa Inés
features.summary: Founded 1804, the last mission of the Santa Bárbara channel group and the nineteenth of the twenty-one.
series: counted in the 1814 friar roster; ministers Tapis & Uría
counted in the census of all 21 missions
named in the Santa Bárbara jurisdiction *estado*
counted in the 1829 statistical report; minister Ordaz

sources.citation: Every row cites its own document in the Archives of California; follow the link to the catalog record.

features.name: Mission San Rafael Arcángel
features.summary: Founded 1817 north of the bay, and one of the two missions the 1828 secularization blueprint proposed to exempt because they lay beyond the San Francisco river.
series: exempted, with San Francisco Solano, from the plan to convert all the missions into pueblos, 'north of the SF river'
C-A 59 (C-A 59) Doc 31 — 'Plan para convertir en pueblos las Misiones de las dos Californias'
counted in the 1829 statistical report; minister Amorós
343 Indians of the new Pueblo de San Rafael received 463 rams, 828 ewes, 97 horses and 343 mares — roughly two rams, three ewes and two equines each
St. Pap., Missions (C-A 50) Doc 457 — *Estado de Bienes semovientes repartidos á los indios*
the linderos of the new Pueblo of San Rafael demarcated by Ignacio Martínez with mayordomo Gregorio Briones, alcalde Jácome Marino and the caporales Camilo and Tiberio
features.result: Counted as a mission, then as a pueblo

features.name: Mission San Francisco Solano (Sonoma)
features.summary: Founded 1823, the twenty-first and last mission and the only one founded under the Mexican republic. Its 1835 padrón is the northernmost settlement count in the Alta California series.
series: exempted, with San Rafael, from the plan to convert all the missions into pueblos
counted in the 1829 statistical report; minister Fortuni
549 souls — the padrón of the Pueblo of Solano (Sonoma)
St. Pap., Missions (C-A 51) Doc 22 — *padrón* of the Pueblo of Solano
